Hi Samir — appreciate the clear asks. I put together a short explainer and attached a line-item example and our latest rate card that shows current SKUs. See attachments: rate_card_v3.pdf and orchid_sample_invoice_apr2027.csv.

High-level summary (short):
- Responses endpoint: billed per-token (input + output) for generation requests; the SKU is model+responses. It replaces many legacy-completions SKUs in the catalog but both can appear on invoices during transitions.
- Chat Completions (legacy): billed per-message+token historically in older rate cards; for most customers we map chat-style payloads onto the Responses SKU for billing continuity, but legacy customers with pinned endpoints may still see old SKUs.
- Legacy endpoints: may show up as separate invoice lines if you used them directly; usage routing (canary/compatibility) can create multiple SKUs in the same invoice month.

Example mapping (attached as a CSV row, reproduced here):
- Scenario: 1 chat thread with 3 messages, 300 input tokens total, 450 output tokens total, model: rw-large-prod
- Billing: Responses.rw-large-prod — tokens: 750 @ unit_price (see rate_card_v3) -> invoice line shows 750 tokens consumed.
- If the same traffic used the legacy chat endpoint (chat.completions.rw-large-prod) you would see chat.completions.rw-large-prod — tokens: 750 (or in some older invoices the platform shows messages:3 and tokens:750). We included both variants in the sample invoice.

Committed discounts: yes — reserved/commit discounts are applied at the SKU level on the invoice. If you commit to a reserved monthly spend, the billing system applies the discount to eligible SKUs (we exclude marketplace-managed SKUs sometimes). For your deal we can ensure the commitment covers Responses and the compatible legacy SKUs; I asked Marcus to validate the SKU list for ORCH-2345.

Next steps:
- Marcus and I attached a one-row CSV showing the mapping.
- If procurement wants, we can run your actual trial month's usage through our mapping and return a redlined sample invoice showing line-by-line translation.
- I'm happy to do a 20-minute call with procurement this week to walk through.

Best,

Tessa Morgan

Adding a very short technical note to make the example concrete for procurement.

- Metering unit: we count tokens at the model pipeline boundary — that includes encoded input tokens + generated tokens. The unit on the invoice is "tokens" for Responses and for most modern SKUs.
- Older chat SKUs sometimes included a secondary "messages" column; that is informational and (in most cases) not used for pricing calculations anymore — cost is token-driven.
- Example numbers (using the current public list price as an example row in the rate card):
  * Responses.rw-large-prod: $0.00035 per token -> 750 tokens = $0.2625 before discounts
  * Chat.completions.rw-large-prod (legacy SKU): $0.00040 per token -> 750 tokens = $0.30 before discounts

Those per-token rows are what will be reconciled against a reserved spend. If Orchid wants the committed discount to cover the legacy SKU while you migrate traffic, we can add an explicit clause in the SOW so finance maps legacy lines to the committed bucket for the duration of the transition. Laura, can you confirm finance/legal ok on that flow?

Thanks,
Marcus
